rows.description: Bullying makes me feel nobody wants me. That belief is what the bully creates, not the truth. I reach for one safe friend or a club where I fit. Isolation grows in secrecy, so I say it aloud.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, contempt, fear, hatred, loyalty, mockery
related mind states: loneliness, trust

rows.description: Classmates laugh at a photo of me in the class group chat. It hurts and feels public. Wise: do not reply in anger, save the screenshot, tell a parent or teacher. It is not my fault and it can be stopped.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, contempt, fear, hatred, loneliness, loyalty
related mind states: amusement, anger, hurt

rows.description: After telling an adult and practising a calm firm voice, I say stop that, I do not like it, and leave. Confidence grows from small brave steps. If it continues, I do not handle it alone; adults step in.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, contempt, fear, hatred, loneliness, loyalty
related mind states: calm

rows.description: I pick on a quieter boy because it makes me feel big and gets laughs. Underneath I may feel small or copy how I am treated at home. Wise change: notice the hurt on his face and stop, then apologise.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fear, guilt, insecurity, shame
related mind states: amusement, contempt, hurt

rows.description: The boy I tease flinches when I come near. Seeing his fear should make me uncomfortable, not proud. The mature step is to stop, say sorry and mean it. Pretending it is only a joke keeps hurting him.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: contempt, guilt, insecurity, shame
related mind states: fear, pride, hurt

rows.description: I copy the older boys who tease others because they seem cool. Belonging through cruelty is a trap. Wise: find a group that likes me without needing a victim. Following the crowd is not the same as being strong.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: contempt, fear, guilt, insecurity, shame
related mind states: nostalgia

rows.description: My mother is told I have been mean and is disappointed. I feel hot with shame and want to hide or blame. A good response is honesty, saying sorry to the child, and asking how to do better. Excuses and blaming the victim make it worse.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: contempt, fear, guilt, insecurity
related mind states: disappointment, shame

rows.description: The teacher calmly asks me what happened and does not shout. I want to lie, but owning it feels lighter. Wise: admit it, repair with the other child, and learn what I was really feeling.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: contempt, fear, guilt, insecurity, shame
related mind states: calm

rows.description: I laughed along at someone and later feel sick about it. Guilt shows my conscience works. I can apologise to him, and next time refuse to join. Guilt that turns to defensiveness teaches nothing.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: contempt, fear, insecurity, shame
related mind states: amusement, guilt

rows.description: I tease others about their looks because I dread being teased myself. Fear of being the target drives me to attack first. A wiser way is to build real confidence and find kinder friends.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: contempt, fear, guilt, shame
related mind states: fear, insecurity
